title: PLA bench leg (motor day)
about: The limits the RS-04 configuration tool (designer/motor-tool.html) and its bridge (rig/rs04_bridge.py) enforce on the PLA bench leg. A number with a 'sources' entry is consumed from that file and checked against it by rig/tests/test_rs04_vectors.py: change the source, never only this copy.

limits.limit_torque_nm.what: the PLA leg's cap from the motor-day derating (docs/motor-day.md)

limits.can_timeout_ticks.name: GP_RS04_CAN_TIMEOUT
limits.can_timeout_ticks.what: 0.1 s without a frame and the motor drops to reset

limits.can_timeout_max_ticks.name: GP_RS04_CAN_TIMEOUT
limits.can_timeout_max_ticks.what: the tool never sets a longer watchdog than the firmware's

jog_basis: The jog limits are the tool's own, chosen for a motor on the bench or a leg in the air: 3 N m is a quarter of the cap and half the continuous torque of the thermal model's bench limit (see references), 1 rad/s is a slow swing an operator can stop by hand on a bare motor, Kp 20 N m/rad reaches the jog torque at 0.15 rad (8.6 deg) of error.
notes: The motor powers up at limit_torque 10 N m, as the motor-day ladder's step L1 saves it (docs/motor-day.md: L1-L3 run at 10); the 12 N m cap is the ceiling the tool lets you write for L4-L7, never stored by Write and read back.

Stop a session when a motor's case passes the bench face limit, and plan held torques under the continuous limit for the room's temperature: both are in the motor heat model's bench section (references: exports/leg/thermal/motor_thermal.json, /bench; docs/motor-thermal.md section 5). This profile does not copy those numbers.
Without --cap, rig.run runs at the 60 N m cap: never on the PLA leg (docs/motor-day.md).

references.what: the PLA bench thermal limits: the face limit and the continuous torque per room temperature
the motor-day test ladder and the PLA cap

changes.what: stores limit_torque 10, as motor-day step L1 does (review of PR #209)
